clue.text: Spirit of additional ace labour leader's in…

indicators.note: in says the ace and the labour leader sit inside the word for additional

parts.note: additional means more, as in more helpings
A is the abbreviation for ace on playing cards

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter, so take the start of labour

explanation.surface: A trailing clue: the spirit of extra-good labour leaders is in... something that the next clue completes.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links to the next clue for the surface only. 'in' puts A plus L (first letter of 'labour') inside MORE; the 's of leader's means 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Morale is the confidence and enthusiasm of a group, its collective spirit.

parts.note: crazy means mad
a rig is an outfit of clothing or equipment
Al Capone was the notorious Chicago gangster, so Al stands for a gangster

explanation.surface: A mad costume worn with a mobster's tune.
explanation.definitionFit: A madrigal is a part-song for several unaccompanied voices, popular in the Renaissance.

clue.text: Send ball hitting net in game

indicators.note: in places the tennis term inside the word for send

parts.note: to route something is to send it by a particular way
in tennis a let is a serve that clips the net and is replayed

explanation.surface: Playing tennis, a serve clips the net during the match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' marks the container. In tennis a let is called when a serve clips the net cord and must be replayed, which is why 'ball hitting net' is fair.
explanation.definitionFit: Roulette is a casino game of chance with a spinning wheel and a ball.

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: to reel in a line is to wind it

explanation.surface: Winding up a wristwatch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses REEL in this down entry. The question mark warns that 'watch' is a loose definition: a leer is a look.
explanation.definitionFit: To leer is to look at someone in a lewd or sly way, a kind of watching.

indicators.note: following places the despair word after the letter for left

parts.note: L is the standard abbreviation for left
despair and anguish are both deep distress

explanation.surface: Completing the previous clue: a party leader falls into despair as the left wing declines.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis is surface glue only; this clue stands alone.
explanation.definitionFit: To languish is to weaken or waste away, a gradual decline in health or vigour.

indicators.note: displaying is a loose signal that the letters are rearranged to show something new

explanation.surface: A performer who shows real quality.
explanation.walkthrough: 'displaying' rearranges GENUINE CLASS. ALEC GUINNESS was a British film actor (Star Wars, The Bridge on the River Kwai).
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Alec Guinness was a celebrated English stage and screen performer.

explanation.surface: A fool's chatter.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as two words, GO ON means to talk at length, which is blathering. The 's means 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A goon is a stupid person, a fool; and to go on is to talk tediously and endlessly.

clue.text: His rise was thwarted by the sun

definitions.text: His rise was thwarted by the sun

parts.words: His rise was thwarted by the sun
parts.note: describes the Greek myth of a boy flying on wings of wax and feathers who soared too close to the sun, which melted them

explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth this son of Daedalus flew too near the sun, his wax wings melted and he fell into the sea.

indicators.note: over in a down clue places the word for wounded above the French article

parts.note: wounded means hurt
le is French for the

explanation.surface: An injured runner beats the French in a race.
explanation.definitionFit: To hurtle is to rush along at great speed, to race.

indicators.note: after puts the word for exploited behind the word for work

parts.note: do means work, as in doing a job
exploited means used, taken advantage of

explanation.surface: Someone who was taken advantage of after a job ended up utterly deflated.
explanation.definitionFit: Doused describes a flame extinguished, which is what blowing out a candle does.

clue.text: Charming young lady reading the news, perhaps

parts.note: a deb (debutante) is a young upper-class woman entering society
a newsreader is on air while broadcasting; perhaps marks this as one example

explanation.surface: A suave young woman presenting the television news bulletin.
explanation.definitionFit: Debonair means suave and urbane, with a confident, charming manner.

clue.text: Plonk an iron drive with mid-air spin

indicators.note: spin signals that the letters are whirled into a new order
mid picks the middle letter of the word air

explanation.surface: A golfer slams an iron shot that spins in the air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mid' takes I from AIR; 'spin' rearranges AN, IRON, DRIVE and I. Plonk is British slang for cheap wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Vin ordinaire is cheap everyday table wine, which British slang calls plonk.

parts.note: I is the abbreviation for independent, as for a politician

indicators.note: back tells us to read the word for settled from right to left

parts.note: to meet a bill is to settle it, so settled gives met

explanation.surface: A self-standing newspaper piece reported after a dispute was resolved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' makes TEM. 'Settled' is a past tense in the bill-paying sense: you settle or meet a debt.
explanation.definitionFit: An item is a single thing or a separate piece in a list or newspaper, an article.

clue.text: Rubbish head of government consumed by bitterness

indicators.note: consumed by says the first letter goes inside the word for bitterness

parts.note: bile is bitterness or bad temper, from the bitter digestive fluid

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, here of government

explanation.surface: A political leader eaten up by resentment and spouting nonsense.
explanation.definitionFit: Bilge is nonsense, worthless talk, from the foul water in a ship's hull.

clue.text: Fight expected before end of bell

indicators.note: before puts the word for expected ahead of the final letter

parts.note: due means expected, as in a train due at noon

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter, here of bell

explanation.surface: A boxing bout anticipated before the final bell rings.
explanation.definitionFit: A duel is a formal combat between two people, a fight.

clue.text: Lifts a chopper up and down

indicators.note: up and down says the word reads the same in either direction of this down entry

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: Raising a helicopter vertically.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole answer is the wordplay: it reads the same from top or bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: The spinning rotary blades are what raise a helicopter into the air.

parts.note: obese means very fat
L is a recognised abbreviation for little

explanation.surface: Is being somewhat overweight a catastrophe?
explanation.definitionFit: Fatal means causing death or ruin, as disastrous does.

indicators.note: shot means ruined or broken up, so the letters are scattered and reassembled

explanation.surface: Somewhere near the stars, a fine shot of the red planet.
explanation.definitionFit: Astronomical relates to the stars and heavenly bodies, as stellar does.

indicators.note: found in says the numeral sits inside the church word

parts.note: a minster is a large church, and some, such as York Minster, are cathedrals
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A clergyman can often be found in a cathedral.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines too: a member of the clergy is someone found in a cathedral.
explanation.definitionFit: A minister is a member of the clergy who serves in a church such as a cathedral.

indicators.note: upset means knocked over, so the letters are tipped into a new order

explanation.surface: A country is upset and becomes the most upset of all.
explanation.definitionFit: Angriest means most furious, the highest degree of being upset.

clue.text: Lacking energy, new diets no one can digest

indicators.note: new signals the letters are put into a fresh order
lacking says the energy letter is missing from the word diets

parts.note: E is the physics abbreviation for energy

explanation.surface: A fad eating plan so feeble that nobody can stomach it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lacking' drops E from DIETS, leaving DITS; 'new' rearranges DITS, NO ONE and CAN. 'digest' looks like a verb about eating but is a noun: a summary.
explanation.definitionFit: A digest is a shortened summary, and condensation is the act or result of shortening a text.

indicators.note: accepted says the lending word takes the abbreviation inside it

parts.note: to advance money is to lend it
e.g. means for example, as does say

explanation.surface: A loan is approved, say, in return for a tale.
explanation.definitionFit: A legend is a traditional story, often about heroes.

explanation.surface: Avoids young women.
explanation.definitionFit: To miss something is to avoid it; and misses are young unmarried women or girls.

indicators.note: backward means the word for tendency is read in reverse

parts.note: a tide is a trend or tendency, as in the tide of opinion

explanation.surface: Inspecting a habit of regression.
explanation.definitionFit: To edit is to check and correct a text before it is published.

indicators.note: swallowing says the phrase Bang! Startled holds the answer within its letters

explanation.surface: A sudden loud noise makes someone jump and gulp down their dread.
explanation.definitionFit: Angst is a deep feeling of anxiety or dread.

indicators.note: they say signals that the word sounds like another

parts.note: to spy is to peer, look closely

explanation.surface: Someone claims an undercover agent is a double agent.
explanation.walkthrough: A mole here is a stone breakwater or jetty, not a spy; the spy surface pushes the other way.
explanation.definitionFit: A mole is a massive harbour wall or jetty, the same kind of structure as a pier.

parts.note: to give is to sag or yield under weight

explanation.surface: Hand over an old-fashioned dessert.
explanation.definitionFit: Sago is a starchy milk pudding made from palm pith grains.

indicators.note: on links the lines of verse to the carbon symbol

parts.note: C is the chemical symbol for carbon
an ode is a poem, lines of verse

explanation.surface: Regulations written about carbon emissions.
explanation.definitionFit: A code is a set of rules, as in a highway code.

clue.text: European community's still on top of the world

parts.note: EC is the abbreviation for the European Community
still means unmoving, static

explanation.surface: The European bloc remains in a state of great happiness.
explanation.definitionFit: Ecstatic means overjoyed, and being on top of the world is an idiom for great happiness.

parts.note: kind and sort both mean type
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, Latin for that is

explanation.surface: Describing what type of person Sally is.
explanation.walkthrough: Sally looks like a woman's name; it is a sudden charge from a besieged position. The 's means 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A sally is a military sortie, a sudden rush out against attackers.

parts.note: a disc is a gramophone record
over means finished, at an end

explanation.surface: A record has come to an end.
explanation.definitionFit: To discover is to find something for the first time.

clue.text: Picked up king's knight on time

parts.note: Lear is the king in Shakespeare's tragedy
N is the chess notation for knight

explanation.surface: Learning chess: the king's knight moves on the clock.
explanation.definitionFit: To pick up a skill or fact is to learn it, so picked up is learnt.
